best_for: Video editors, archivists and anyone troubleshooting playback who needs to see exactly which codec, bit rate, frame rate and color settings a file uses.
description:
MediaInfo is a file inspector from MediaArea.net, a small company that also makes archive and video quality tools such as MediaConch and QCTools. It is open source under a BSD-style license.

Open a file and it tells you how it was made: H.264, HEVC or FFV1 video, AC3, DTS, AAC or FLAC audio, whether the picture is interlaced, and its chroma subsampling. It also reads tags such as ID3, Vorbis comments and APE, so you see the title, album and track number, and it lists subtitle and caption tracks from SRT and ASS to CEA-608. It even reads unprotected DVD and Blu-ray structures. You can tailor what each view shows, and MediaInfoOnline lets you try it on a file without installing anything.

points.title: Shows what is inside a file
points.text: MediaInfo reports container, video, audio, subtitle and chapter details: codec, duration, bit rate, frame rate, color space, bit depth, sample rate and channels. It reads MP4, QuickTime, Matroska, AVI, MXF, MPEG-TS and more.

points.title: Four views, three exports
points.text: You can view results as text, a sheet, a tree or HTML, and export to text, CSV or HTML. The CSV export helps when you need to check a whole folder of files.

points.title: GUI, command line and library
points.text: The same engine comes as a desktop app, a command-line tool and a library, so you can script checks once you know which fields you need. It also hooks into the file manager through drag and drop and the context menu.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: MediaInfo uses a BSD-style license and asks for donations rather than charging. Free support covers only the newest release; backports for older versions are a paid service.

points.title: A setting sends anonymous stats
points.text: With Check for newest version turned on, the app contacts mediaarea.net and sends anonymous usage statistics. Turn the option off to stop it.

points.title: Verified Flatpak, all-user Windows installer
points.text: The Flathub package for x64 and Arm64 is verified as published by MediaArea. Windows installers cover 32-bit, x64 and Arm64 and install for all users.

points.title: History lives on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 32 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so older builds there need another source.
